background.speaker: SPEAKER_01
background.text: No, early in the election cycle, you seem to think that he was not â that he could be beaten, that there were a lot of conservatives out there. I think at one point your line was, with Trump we lose. So what happened? Why was he able to hold on and do away with this field faster than just about anybody would have expected? And is it that the voters have changed and they're no longer looking for that type of [target], Mitt Romney, George W. Bush vision?

ground_truth: I think it's a bunch of things. I think it's partly what you said. They want a fighter, they want a scrapper, they want a cultural warrior. I also think these indictments, particularly the New York ones, made him a victim. And that grafted MAGA onto him that much more. Look, I think these federal indictments are far more serious. I think these New York ones are far more political in nature. If his name was Don Smith, I'm not sure that he would have been indicted. I don't doubt that he cooked the books and paid off the porn star, but I don't think he would probably have gotten indicted for these things if he was just some other citizen. My point being is, these indictments made him a victim. It gave him a very credible victim narrative, and that more grafted MAGA onto him. People want to see a fighter. Yes, he was able to dispatch, and he sucks the oxygen out of the room with news. He can dominate news cycles. And that made it really hard for a lot of these primary opponents to really catch up. I don't think he was able to catch fire. And you could argue we had too many, we had a big field that was too big for too long. Nikki's still hanging around the hoop, and I'm glad she's there. But I also think that our party has changed. We have a party that is really dominated by Trump populism, and that is cultural war populism. It's zero-sum game politics. So it's not conservatism as I would describe it, classical liberal conservatism, where a party is based on principles and policies that achieve goals and ends that are timeless. And then that can have a lot of people that could become the champion of those principles. It's really a party dominated by the cult of personality of Trump, the zero-sum game politics that gets played off of that, the fact that he has been victimized more or less. And so that, I think, has made it harder for the, let's just say, the 40% base to leave him. And so he was going into this primary with a very good sticky base. The reason I always made the electability argument is we do lose with him. He only won 2016. That's the only election he's ever won. And then we lost the House. We lost the Senate. We lost the Senate and the House again. And I still think that's probably the better likelihood. But the other part of this, I'll give you a quick answer, is Biden is so weak. That's a problem. For those of us who say we lose with Trump, it's a harder argument to make these days. Because of Biden's inherent weakness. And so even Trump is beating Biden in the polls these days. And I think that's more of a testament to how weak Biden is than how strong Trump is. Look at the Marquette poll in Wisconsin. Nikki Haley beats Biden by double digits in Wisconsin and in other states. Trump beats Biden by one point. So I still think there's a big delta, a difference between pick your Republican, not named Trump. Let's just go with Nikki Haley. Nikki Haley destroys Biden, wins the House, wins the Senate in a general election. With Trump, because of Biden being so weak, he still barely edges out Biden in the polls, makes it a close election. I think at the end of the day, Democrats come home, not because they're motivated by Biden, but because they're motivated by Trump. And in those swing states, mine is one of those, let's just say, five states, that suburban voter still probably won't vote for Trump. The question is, will they vote for Biden like they did in 2020, or will they just do some third vote? I don't know. I don't know. I don't know. I don't know. I don't know. I don't know. I don't know. I don't know. I don't know. I don't know. Some third party thing or write-in or something like that. That's the question that I don't know.
